title: Project Manager - Technical Assistance
description: 🌱 We’re hiring: Project Manager – Technical Assistance (Ethiopia) 🌱 Organisation: COLEAD Programme: Mobilizing Actors in Horticulture for Entrepreneurship and Boosting Ethiopian Resilience (MAHEBER) Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Start date: As soon as possible Contract: Independent consultancy agreement - 1 year (renewable) About COLEAD & the programme COLEAD is a non-profit interprofessional association founded in 1973 whose mission is to support the sustainable transformation of agri-food systems and strengthen the contribution of the agri-food sector to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). COLEAD manages development programmes in more than 50 countries across Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific, supporting private-sector operators, producer organisations, public institutions and other stakeholders to improve competitiveness, sustainability and market access. As part of the implementation of the MAHEBER Programme – “Mobilizing Actors in Horticulture for Entrepreneurship and Boosting Ethiopian Resilience”, COLEAD is recruiting a Project Manager within its Technical Assistance Department. MAHEBER aims to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of Ethiopia’s horticulture sector by supporting stakeholders in adapting to evolving sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS), commercial, social and environmental requirements in local, regional and international markets. The Role Based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the Project Manager will work under the supervision of the MAHEBER Programme Coordinator and in close collaboration with COLEAD teams in Addis Ababa, Nairobi, Brussels and Lomé. The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of partner-beneficiaries and coordinate technical assistance and capacity-building activities supporting horticultural businesses, producer organisations, public institutions and support-service providers. The role requires strong project management skills, experience in the Ethiopian agricultural or horticultural sector, and the ability to translate identified needs into practical and impactful support interventions. Key responsibilities Assess support requests from partner-beneficiaries and identify priority needs, challenges and capacity-building opportunities. Develop and manage tailored support projects, including the implementation of COLEAD’s Sustainability Self-Assessment System (SAS). Coordinate technical assistance, training and other capacity-building activities from planning through implementation, monitoring and follow-up. Prepare terms of reference, support the selection and contracting of experts and service providers, and supervise the delivery of assignments. Coordinate with programme partners and stakeholders to ensure effective technical, administrative and logistical implementation of activities. Organise and monitor calls for expressions of interest and other beneficiary selection processes. Ensure activities are delivered on time, to the required quality standards, and in accordance with COLEAD and donor procedures. Contribute to programme monitoring, evaluation and reporting, including activity documentation, financial follow-up and performance tracking. Maintain strong relationships with horticultural companies, producer organisations, public institutions, experts and other programme stakeholders. Contribute to workshops, conferences, trade fairs, training resources and other programme activities. Profile Master’s degree (or equivalent) in agriculture, agronomy, horticulture, agribusiness, project management, or a related field. Minimum 7 years’ relevant professional experience, including substantial experience in Ethiopia’s agricultural or horticultural sector and at least 3 years in project management. Experience designing, implementing, and monitoring technical assistance, capacity-building, or organisational development activities. Strong understanding of horticultural value chains and experience working with businesses, producer organisations, public institutions, and support-service providers. Experience managing external experts and service providers, as well as project monitoring, reporting, and administrative follow-up. Strong project management, analytical, organisational, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a multicultural environment. Good digital literacy and fluency in English and Amharic. Knowledge of French, Spanish, or Portuguese is an asset. Conditions 📍 Full-time position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia ✈️ Regular travel within Ethiopia and occasional travel within the Eastern African region and Belgium may be required 📆 Start date: As soon as possible 📩 How to Apply Send your CV + Cover Letter + References by Friday 16th of October 2026 17:00 CEST . Joining COLEAD means joining a multicultural and committed team working to promote sustainable and inclusive agri-food systems. It is an opportunity to contribute to meaningful development impact

title: Senior Technical Advisor – Neonatal Respiratory Care
description: Overview The Senior Technical Advisor – Neonatal Respiratory Care will lead the execution of a 24-month project funded by the Gates Foundation focused on Ethiopia's national scale-up of newborn respiratory care. Operating within Jhpiego's role as a neutral delivery integrator, the Senior Technical Advisor will work closely with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and key health partners to transition from fragmented CPAP device procurement to a coordinated, sustainably financed national system. The primary objective is to facilitate the co-design and delivery of a government-endorsed National Neonatal Respiratory Care Investment Roadmap. This position will manage the local landscape mapping, convene stakeholder validation mechanisms, and lead the secretariat for the government-led Investment Coordination Forum across bubble CPAP (bCPAP), medical oxygen systems, and pulse oximetry. Contract Type - Fixed Term Contract for One Year Responsibilities Technical Leadership & Roadmap Co-Design Oversee Phase 1 (Ecosystem Mapping & Landscape Analysis) and Phase 2 (Validation & Roadmap Development) in Ethiopia. Direct the technical analysis of Ethiopia's newborn care landscape, focusing on CPAP expansion across Level 2 Small and Sick Newborn Care (SSNC) facilities, oxygen availability, pulse oximetry, and supply chain constraints. Ensure CPAP (including Vayu and Diamedica devices), oxygen, and monitoring tools are integrated into a single clinical package alongside cross-cutting needs (workforce training, equipment maintenance, and digital health data systems). Lead the drafting, refinement, and finalization of the government-endorsed National Neonatal Respiratory Care Investment Roadmap. Stakeholder Engagement & Government Facilitation Serve as Jhpiego’s primary technical focal point to the Ministry of Health (MOH) and regional health bureaus for this investment. Provide technical and secretariat support to establish and institutionalize the government-led Investment Coordination Forum. Facilitate national co-design workshops, pulse surveys, and consensus-building sessions with donors, implementing partners, procurement agencies, and professional associations to align funding and eliminate parallel implementation. Program Monitoring, Learning & Reporting Document key learnings, success factors, and operational bottlenecks throughout the roadmap development process. Organize thematic learning exchanges and participate in regional virtual roundtables to share Ethiopia’s experiences with peer countries. Track project deliverables, manage grant reporting requirements, and ensure compliance with Jhpiego and donor guidelines. Required Qualifications Education: Advanced degree (Master’s or MD) in Public Health, Medicine (Pediatrics/Neonatology preferred), Health Systems Management, or related field. Experience: 9 - 10 years of professional experience leading maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) or health systems strengthening programs in Ethiopia. Demonstrated track record of working collaboratively with the Ministry of Health (MOH), regional health bureaus, and international donors (e.g., Gates Foundation, Department of State). Direct experience in clinical newborn care interventions, Level 2 SSNC scale-up, or biomedical technology/equipment delivery systems. Experience conducting health facility landscape analyses, policy synthesis, or drafting national strategy documents and investment plans. Core Competencies Stakeholder Facilitation: Strong ability to convene diverse stakeholders, mediate competing priorities, and foster government ownership. Analytical & Writing Skills: Exceptional capacity to synthesize complex healthcare data, facility assessments, and financial projections into clear technical reports and strategic roadmaps. Language: Professional fluency in English and Amharic Knowledge of additional Ethiopian languages is an advantage Salary: Between 28,659 – 47,848 USD per annum. Jhpiego offers competitive salaries and a comprehensive employee benefits package. title: Veterinary Medicine Professional
description: Company Description Nathan Dairy Farm is a growing agricultural business located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with a focus on sustainable dairy production and high standards of animal welfare. The farm maintains a mixed herd and emphasizes modern herd management practices to ensure consistent milk quality and productivity. Team members collaborate closely to improve animal health, optimize feeding programs, and adopt evidence-based practices. The organization values professionalism, continuous learning, and a safe working environment for both people and animals. Role Description This full-time Veterinary Medicine Professional role is a hybrid position based at Nathan Dairy Farm in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with some flexibility for work from home on administrative and planning tasks. The professional will oversee the clinical health of the herd, including routine examinations, diagnosis and treatment of illness, and implementation of preventive health programs such as vaccination, parasite control, and biosecurity measures. Daily responsibilities include monitoring animal behavior and welfare, advising on nutrition and housing conditions, performing minor surgical procedures when required, and maintaining accurate medical records. The role also involves training farm staff on animal handling and health protocols, collaborating on breeding and herd improvement strategies, and supporting compliance with relevant veterinary and agricultural regulations. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong skills in Animal Care and Animal Health for herd monitoring, welfare management, and preventive care. Candidates should possess solid knowledge of Medicine and Veterinary Surgery for diagnosis, treatment, and basic surgical interventions in dairy cattle. Candidates should possess effective Communication skills for educating farm staff, documenting health plans, and coordinating with external veterinary and regulatory bodies. Veterinary degree (DVM or equivalent) and valid authorization to practice veterinary medicine in Ethiopia or eligibility to obtain it. Experience working with dairy cattle or large animals in a farm or clinical setting is highly beneficial. Ability to interpret laboratory results, use diagnostic tools, and apply evidence-based veterinary practices. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to work safely in a farm environment with a collaborative mindset.

title: Finance Director
description: Management Sciences for Health (MSH) is seeking a Finance Director for two U.S. Government (USG)-funded projects in Ethiopia: Implementing the America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS) and the Supply Chain Strengthening (SCS) projects. MSH is a global health nonprofit that makes foundational changes to health systems to protect people from diseases and improve their health. MSH collaborates with local partners, from ministries of health to communities, to strengthen and complement existing health systems. Since 1971, MSH has worked in more than 150 countries to help ensure sustainable, resilient, and equitable access to quality health care around the globe. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

As countries prepare for and adapt to population ageing, we are seeking to make a difference at a critical juncture to how societies, economies and institutions adapt to this change. Our Strategy 2030, Ageing in a Just World, sets out how we will work to shape the future we all share. By working together with our partners, we aim to inspire a movement for change. By ensuring all our work promotes older people’s wellbeing, dignity and voice, we seek to transform the lives of older people now and in the future. Guided by our commitment to our values of impact, learning, partnership, and inclusion, we partner with others to bring systemic change and impact at scale. By acting as a supporter, convenor and thought leader, we want to make an impact that matters for older people and their communities. Our organisational culture The culture of the organisation aims to ensure: Accountability for All: Every individual and team member is responsible for their actions and decisions, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities and commitments to partners and network members. Trust, Respect, and Inclusion: We strive to create an environment where mutual trust is the foundation of all relationships, diverse perspectives are valued, and everyone feels included in decision-making processes. Culture of Collaboration: Working together across teams, network members, and partners to share knowledge, maximise impact, and drive collective success, rather than working in silos. Openness and Transparency: Ensuring open communication, clear decision-making processes and actions, and a commitment to sharing information in a way that builds trust and accountability. Collective Responsibilities Within and With Partners and Network: Recognising that achieving our mission requires shared responsibility, we promote joint ownership of decisions, initiatives, and outcomes across HelpAge and its network members and partners. Staff and network members are valued: Staff and network members are recognised, and valued and appreciated for their contributions, fostering an environment where every individual feels respected, supported, and integral to our mission, with their input and expertise recognised as vital to achieving our shared goals. At the heart of our work is a thriving, resilient HelpAge global network—a powerful collective of national civil society actors driving change that is rooted in the priorities and experiences of older people. We lead the delivery of HelpAge’s strategic approach to support, convene, and influence, across humanitarian and development contexts, to achieve lasting and inclusive impact. This role will lead and be accountable for the development and delivery of the HelpAge network strategy, ensuring alignment with our global mission and enabling inclusive, sustainable collaboration across the HelpAge network. They lead through the Regional Advisers rather than delivering regional workstreams personally: setting annual priorities and deliverables for each region, in alignment with organisational priorities, and hold Regional Advisers accountable for delivery through regular performance management and review. This is an evolving role. The postholder ensures the capacity strengthening and localisation offer is shaped by what members themselves identify as their needs and differentiated by region and member segment, rather than applied uniformly. They lead the mechanisms that connect global and regional levels of the network - regional convenings, member-to-member exchange, and the flow of regional intelligence into global strategy, positioning and funding decisions. The role works in close partnership with internal stakeholders - Executive Leadership Group, Board, Leadership Group, and Team Heads - and external stakeholders including network members, civil society organisations, local consortia, donors, and institutional partners. The postholder leads the preparation and quality of Governance Committee submissions and Board papers on network development and engagement. Alongside this regional remit, the role holder will lead directly on coordinating members in the Europe region, and work closely with the Head of Advocacy and Evidencing to develop our strategic niche on donor advocacy in Europe. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To make an impact and influence, the role holder will shape and deliver the HelpAge network strategy and HelpAge's transition to locally led ways of working; provide strategic oversight of network member engagement, localisation, and the organisational capacity sharing strategy; lead HelpAge's support to country transitions, including Ukraine; and build an inclusive, resilient and effective global network of local and national organisations. Lead the Thriving Network Impact Vehicle (one of six priority areas through which HelpAge delivers its strategy; the other five target external policy change - social pensions, health coverage, humanitarian action, legal rights, climate adaptation - while this one targets the health and sustainability of the network itself) and its results framework, ensuring a clear connection between day-to-day activities and HelpAge's 2030 network targets, and reporting quarterly to the senior leadership team on progress. Lead delivery of the Network Capacity Sharing Strategy, translating it into a coherent network-wide offer, integrated across programmes, in collaboration with Programme Support, Advocacy and Evidencing and other relevant teams. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Education Bachelor's degree required. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Application Deadline 05 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

description:
Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy Title: Provision of Vehicle Rental Services Objective of the Consultancy This consultancy has the following objective: 1. To secure reliable transportation services for staff coordinating and supporting the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project Background Project Reference: - Donor reference: DN01983 About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN/ About the Project The project focuses on promoting catchment protection through Nature-based Solutions (NbS), framed as best adaptive practices in the context of climate change and increasing land degradation. It aims to scale up NbS for watershed restoration in alignment with national basin development, land degradation neutrality, and landscape restoration goals. The general objective is to enhance water-related ecosystem services in key watersheds of the Awash sub-basin for the benefit of both people and the environment through the application of NbS. To achieve this, the project will strengthen action-oriented partnerships among community-based organizations (CBOs), the wider public, national and local governments, and non-government actors. These partnerships will promote NbS that build knowledge, shape positive attitudes, and encourage good practices, mobilizing society as a whole to achieve large-scale watershed rehabilitation, restoration, and sustainable development and use. The general objective of the project is to improve ground water recharge of the little Akaki catchment of the upper Awash river basin focusing on Guleel & Addis Ketema sub-cities of Addis Ababa and Sululta town of Sheger city, specifically in Bilisuma micro catchment. Description of the Assignment The overall objective of this procurement is to competitively select and contract qualified vehicle rental or leasing service provider(s) capable of providing reliable, safe, well-maintained, and appropriately insured vehicles to support the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project. The selected service provider(s) will provide vehicles based on the operational requirements of IUCN. Scope of Work The selected service provider shall provide vehicle rental and/or lease services to IUCN in accordance with the agreed requirements and on a call-off basis, as and when required. The services may include, but are not limited to, the following: Vehicle Provision The selected service provider shall provide safe, reliable, well-maintained, and roadworthy vehicles that meet IUCN’s operational and field-activity requirements. Vehicles shall be suitable for both urban and off-road travel and shall comply with all applicable Ethiopian legal, safety, registration, insurance, and roadworthiness requirements. Vehicle Condition and Standards The primary vehicle category required under this procurement is: Toyota Hilux Double Cab 4x4 – 2.8L Diesel, model year 2020 or newer. Vehicles offered shall be in good mechanical and physical condition, regularly serviced and maintained, and equipped with all standard safety features and legally required documentation. IUCN reserves the right to inspect and approve vehicles prior to deployment and to reject any vehicle that does not meet the agreed specifications or required safety and operational standards. 2. Drivers Where vehicles are provided with drivers, the service provider shall ensure that drivers: Have updated CVs and hold valid and appropriate driving licenses. Have relevant experience and familiarity with Ethiopian road and traffic conditions. Demonstrate safe and professional driving practices. Comply with IUCN security and safety requirements. Maintain professional conduct when interacting with IUCN staff, partners, consultants, and other passengers. 3. Geographic Coverage and terms of service To establish high operational predictability and commercial confidence for the selected Vendor, IUCN defines the service framework under the following mandatory terms: Contract Duration : The baseline framework agreement shall remain valid for a fixed period of Six (6) months , subject to satisfactory performance and potential project timeline extensions. Service Frequency : Vehicle deployment will operate on an occasional, "as-needed" project basis rather than continuous, uninterrupted daily operations over the 6-month period. Minimum Utilization Guarantee : To secure the Vendor’s revenue stability, IUCN guarantees a minimum billing and deployment commitment of four (4) operational days per week for any week in which the vehicle service is activated or called up. Rate Cap Consistency for Additional Days : If project demands require the vehicle to be utilized beyond the 4-day minimum in a given week (up to 7 days), the Vendor agrees to maintain the exact same pro-rated daily rate established for the baseline minimum contract days. No premium, overtime surcharge, or inflated short-term rates shall apply for these additional active days. 4. Responsibilities of the Service Provider and Work Norms The selected service provider shall: Provide suitable vehicles according to agreed specifications. Ensure all vehicles are properly maintained and roadworthy. Ensure that all required legal documentation and insurance remain valid throughout the contract period. Provide qualified drivers where required. Ensure timely replacement of vehicles in case of mechanical failure or other operational issues. Respond promptly to IUCN transport requirements. Maintain appropriate communication with the designated IUCN focal person. Ensure compliance with applicable health, safety, security, environmental, and legal requirements. Provide accurate invoices and supporting documentation for services provided. Immediately inform IUCN of any incidents, accidents, delays, or issues affecting the delivery of services. Duration of the Assignment The duration of the vehicle rental/lease agreement will be Six- months . The contract may include an option for extension subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funding, and IUCN procurement procedures. Deliverables and Activities The consultant will provide the following deliverables and carry out the following activities: Deliverable/Activity - Description - Timeline Contract Signing and Mobilization - Signing of the contract and confirmation of vehicle availability - November 10th 2026 Vehicle Deployment - Deployment of vehicles according to IUCN requirements - November 15th 2026 Provision of Transport Services - Continuous provision of vehicle rental/lease services as requested - Throughout contract period Maintenance and Replacement - Regular maintenance and timely replacement of vehicles when required - Throughout contract period and at-least on a quarterly basis Service Reporting and Invoicing - Submission of service records and invoices - Monthly Contract Completion - Completion of services and final reporting - April 2027 Payment Schedule The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant. Deliverable - Payment Arrangement Vehicle rental/lease services- Payment based on agreed rates and actual services provided Monthly service provision - Subject to submission and approval of invoice and supporting documentation Additional approved services, if any - Payment based on agreed rates and prior approval by IUCN Skills and Experience The consultant must have the following skills, education and experience as a minimum: Valid business registration and trade license authorizing vehicle rental, leasing, transport, or related services. Relevant experience in providing vehicle rental or leasing services. Availability of a suitable fleet of vehicles. Proven experience providing services to organizations, development partners, government institutions, NGOs, or private sector clients. Supervision and coordination The consultant will report to and work under the supervision of the Regional Procurement and Operations Manager.

Leadership in proposal design and development, ensuring timely submission and providing inputs when applicable. Remaining aware of donor funding intention. Establish country partnerships to allow for collective organizations efforts through consortia. Work with Senior Management Team (SMT) to ensure the coordination of programs. description:
PLEASE NOTE: This search is being conducted by Ethiojobs. Please apply DIRECTLY through the link below : https://ethiojobs.net/job/UAVcbgg81M-government-relations-advisor-africa-vital-strategies _________________ Vital Strategies is an international public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury and death. We currently work in 73 countries, supporting data-driven decision making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include non-communicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, obesity prevention, overdose prevention, environmental health, and vital statistics systems building. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. The candidate must have authorization to work legally in the respective country at the time of hire. Vital Strategies offers highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position will vary by location, experience and qualifications. Duties and Responsibilities: Regional program coordination and strategic vision - · In coordination with the global team, facilitate regional exchanges and development of regional partnerships and a consistent strategy for government engagement and partnership building in the region; · Initiate and/or sustain government partnerships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and other national and regional institutions in priority countries; · Support project launches and startups in new countries within the region, including support for staff recruitment; · Support country teams in translating strategy into implementation plans, including identification of key capacity gaps to be filled, and government engagement needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of program activities; · Identify and participate in regional opportunities and events that help elevate lead poisoning on national agendas; · Promote multisectoral collaboration and partnership-driven approaches to environmental health policy development; · Manage relationships with regional organizations engaged in lead-related activities, and develop, where appropriate, formal or contractual relationships for discrete programmatic activities in support of the initiative. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Qualifications: Education & Degree - · Master’s degree in public health, public policy/Administration, Global Health, international development, environmental health science, or related field. Skills & Abilities - · Strong government engagement and partnership-building skills, with the ability to establish and sustain relationships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and regional institutions; · Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-country initiatives and facilitate regional exchange and collaboration; · Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate regional strategy into actionable country-level implementation plans; · Strong stakeholder management skills across government, NGOs, multilateral agencies, and technical partners; · Ability to promote and facilitate multisectoral collaboration and policy dialogue; · Ability to monitor program quality, performance, and outcomes across a regional portfolio; · Ability to coordinate and engage program stakeholders and other country teams; · Demonstrated sensitivity in handling confidential information; · Proven ability to interpret public health data, generate actionable insights, and support policy recommendations; · Exhibits strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines; demonstrates personal integrity, credibility, and professionalism while taking initiative and making sound, informed decisions in a fast-paced environment; · Professional oral and written proficiency in English; · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to an interdisciplinary international team; · Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook); · Experience working with a geographically distributed team with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, communicate clearly and regularly, monitor performance, and inspire, engage, and motivate staff; · Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment. Experience: Required - · Minimum of eight years of experience in government engagement and public health programming, ideally with experience in health policy, environmental health, and/or global health, especially related to lead poisoning prevention or environmental pollution; · Experience in representing organizations with governments, international institutions, and senior stakeholder forums; · Experience managing multi-country programs in Africa; · Experience working with government agencies, regulatory bodies, and public health facilities; · Experience with program reporting and monitoring. Preferred - · Demonstrated experience in communicating scientific and health information to varied audiences; · Experience in using project management platforms. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: · If hired in Ghana, Rwanda, or Tanzania, the candidate will be hired via Vital Strategies’ Employer of Record on a remote schedule; · The position will require travel up to 30% of the time to visit operating countries in the region to visit field implementation or attend meetings with partners; · The candidate needs to be willing to work with colleagues across different time zones.

description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

description:
What we do
 
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) works worldwide to provide humanitarian protection and assistance to people affected by conflict and armed violence. We take action in response to emergencies and at the same time promote respect for international humanitarian law. We are an independent and neutral organization, and our mandate stems essentially from the Geneva Conventions of 1949. We work closely with National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and with their International Federation in order to ensure a concerted, rational and rapid humanitarian response to the needs of the victims of armed conflict or any other situation of internal violence. We direct and coordinate the international activities conducted in these situations.
 Purpose
 
Language is at the heart of humanitarian action; it enables dialogue, builds trust, and ensures that people affected by conflict can express themselves and be heard.
 
The ICRC Interpreter plays a critical role in enabling this by facilitating accurate and meaningful communication among ICRC delegates, affected populations, authorities, and other stakeholders. Through interpretation in sensitive and complex contexts, including protection activities, visits to detainees, family reunification processes, and dialogue with parties to conflict, the Interpreter ensures that every conversation can take place with clarity, respect, and confidentiality.
 
This is a unique, people-centered role that goes beyond translating words. It requires judgment, cultural awareness, and a deep understanding of the humanitarian principles guiding the ICRC’s work, helping build bridges of understanding where communication can make a real difference.
 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 

Oral interpretation: from Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya to English and vice versa during confidential interviews with people deprived of liberty, ICRC institutional dissemination, ICRC dialogue with authorities, activities to establish the family links which includes delivering Red Cross messages, family tracing and visits to families of detainees.
Written translation: translation of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya languages (newspaper articles, correspondence, etc.) into written English.
Analysis and reporting as required: analysis of conditions of detention, security and other matters relating to the ICRC's mandate.
Can be asked to provide support on other protection activities as needed.

 Relationships
 

Externally, interacts with the authorities, representatives of other organizations and beneficiaries, both within and outside places of detention. May be called upon to develop a network of contacts related to operational needs.
Internally, interacts with staff in other departments.

 Required profile and skills
 

Excellent command of English (C1) required
Excellent command of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya (C1) required
Proficiency in at least two of the above languages is considered a strong asset.
Proficiency in other ICRC operational languages (English, French, Spanish, Russian, Arabic, Portuguese) is a strong asset.
2 years of professional experience. Previous interpreter or translator experience is an advantage.
Strongly motivated by humanitarian work.
Able to work under pressure in a potentially dangerous environment.
Open-minded and adaptable.
University education/degree in interpretation or translation is an advantage.

 Our operational & field constraints
 

In line with the principle of neutrality, the ICRC does not assign personnel to a country of which they are nationals.
Candidates must be in good health and will have to do a medical check-up prior to departure in the field.
Candidates must possess a driving licence (for manual transmission vehicles).
Candidates must be prepared to accept unaccompanied postings (i.e. no spouse, partner, children or dependents) for the first two missions (minimum 12 months each)  or total of 24 months.

 What we offer
 

Rewarding work in a humanitarian and multicultural environment
A two-week orientation course and other opportunities for further in-house training
Attractive social benefits
Join an ICRC talent pool and be considered for future assignments elsewhere

The ICRC values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates!
 Our values
 
At the ICRC, we value impact, collaboration, respect, and compassion. We seek candidates who demonstrate behaviors based on these shared values. For more information on the ICRC values, please visit this page.
 Additional information

Working rate: 100%
Starting date: Continuous, global deployment roster.
Location: Ethiopia, various sites
Hardship : Variable
Job level: B2
Length of assignment: 12 months, extendable
